translation.en:
Your Honour,

Highly Honoured Sir, Court Councillor.

Your Honour's most highly esteemed letter I received today by express, my joy was at first without bounds to know you as my [uncertain: cousin/weather] in [uncertain: Breiten], but on reading your friendly letter further, fresh sorrow stunned my heart, so that I could scarcely compose myself. I have a plan by which I may be rescued out of all embarrassments, only 1800 Rthl of interest must be paid, before that I cannot come to Breslau or into those parts. Honour and fortune are not yet at stake there; I am at present dreadfully disgraced by the eternally accursed von der Lahr affair and cannot show myself there before the 1800 Rthl of interest are paid. Then I can appear there and carry out my plan. If the Most Serene Lord does not help me with this trifle, then may God stand by my forsaken children; I shall then go to another place, where I shall not require His Serene Highness's help. I have sent His Serene Highness the letter which my daughter, in despair after the distraint over the von der Lahr debt, wrote to my youngest son; and if such a cry of lamentation does not move the Lord, if he does not help me with this trifle, then all gentle feelings have ever been strangers to him. Dear friend — it is 1800 Rthl that can save me from shame and mockery, indeed from ruin; these determine my [uncertain: choice] or my woe — I must have them, for before that I shall not come there — If the Prince rescues

me thereby, then I shall appear there vindicated, though not without a summons. I shall then carry out my cause with honour — dismember a part of my estates, assign my children the interest for their maintenance, and then go to the King, where I shall remain until much has been accomplished. This is my plan and these are the consequences, if the Prince finds counsel in the matter of the 1800 Rthl — If this last does not happen, then I can no longer appear there but shall go to Königsberg and from there perhaps to hell. My heart could burst when I consider my misfortune, which I suffer so undeservedly.

Here the estates are sequestrated through the rumour which I endured in Berlin on account of the eternal von der Lahr affair; there now [uncertain: geschwemmen] — but where am I to turn? [uncertain: Schweineren] can be saved with 1800 Rthl and I be put in a position to carry out all my plans — Here too it would prepare blessed consequences. People would deal more sparingly with me, once I had [uncertain: Schweine] free again; and so everything there depends upon the speedy help of His Serene Highness. I would gladly sacrifice to him in return all life's happiness and everything, if only the Lord will do this for me. Take care, then, Your Honour, if it is in any way possible for you in this world, and procure counsel soon, for then I can depart from here on the 12th of September and be at Schlawenschitz about the 16th — but without this help I abandon everything. With a grateful heart and true esteem I shall ever be

Your Honour's

Kontop, the 31st of August

1809.

faithfully devoted friend and servant

v. Triebenfeld

summary_en: A desperate appeal to a Court Councillor to obtain 1,800 Rthl of interest from the Prince, without which Triebenfeld says he cannot show himself in Breslau, disgraced by the von der Lahr affair and by a distraint that has left his estates sequestrated. He encloses mention of a despairing letter from his daughter, and sets out his plan: to clear himself, break up part of his estates for his children's maintenance, and appeal to the King. Otherwise he will go to Königsberg.
summary_de: Dringende Bitte an den Hofrat, beim Fürsten 1800 Rthl Zinsen zu erwirken: ohne diese Summe könne Triebenfeld wegen der Affäre von der Lahr, der Pfändung und des dadurch ausgelösten Gerüchts, das die Sequestration der Güter nach sich zog, nicht in Breslau erscheinen. Mit dem Geld wolle er einen Teil seiner Güter abtrennen, den Kindern die Zinsen zum Unterhalt zuweisen und sich an den König wenden; sonst gehe er nach Königsberg. Beigelegt ein Verzweiflungsbrief seiner Tochter an den jüngsten Sohn. Abreise am 12. September, Ankunft in Schlawenschitz um den 16.
